# Sirach Chapter 10 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 10

---

**1** A wise judge educates his people, and good government flows from the understanding of its rulers.

**2** As the ruler of a people is, so are his officials; as the head of a city is, so are all its inhabitants.

**3** An undisciplined king ruins his people, but a city is built up through the wisdom of its rulers.

**4** The government of the earth is in the hand of the Lord, and he will raise up over it the right person at the right time.

**5** Human success is in the hand of the Lord; it is he who confers dignity on those who make the law.

**6** Do not be resentful of your neighbor for any wrong, and do not act arrogantly in anything you do.

**7** Arrogance is hateful before the Lord and before people, and injustice is offensive to both.

**8** Sovereignty passes from nation to nation on account of violence, arrogance, and greed.

**9** Why should dust and ashes be arrogant? Even now in life the body is decaying.

**10** A long illness mocks the physician; a person is a king today and dead tomorrow.

**11** For when a person dies, they become the inheritance of worms and maggots and decay.

**12** The beginning of human pride is to forsake the Lord; the heart has turned away from him who made it.

**13** For pride is the root of sin, and those who cling to it will pour out abomination; therefore the Lord will bring upon them extraordinary disasters and will utterly overthrow them.

**14** The Lord has toppled the thrones of rulers and has set the lowly in their place.

**15** The Lord has uprooted the proud nations and has planted the humble in their place.

**16** The Lord has laid waste the lands of the nations and has destroyed them to the foundations of the earth.

**17** He has swept some of them away and destroyed them, and has wiped out all memory of them from the earth.

**18** Pride was not created for human beings, nor fierce anger for those born of women.

**19** What kind deserves honor? Those who fear the Lord. What kind deserves dishonor? Those who transgress his commandments.

**20** Among brothers and sisters, a leader is worthy of honor; and those who fear the Lord are worthy of honor in his sight.

**21** The fear of the Lord is the beginning of his acceptance; obstinacy and arrogance are the beginning of rejection.

**22** Rich, renowned, and poor — the glory of all of them is the fear of the Lord.

**23** It is not right to despise a poor person who has understanding, nor is it fitting to honor a sinful person.

**24** The great, the judge, and the ruler are all worthy of honor, but none of them is greater than the one who fears the Lord.

**25** Free citizens will serve an intelligent servant, and a person of understanding will not complain about it.

**26** Do not make a display of your wisdom in your work, and do not show your cleverness at an unsuitable time.

**27** Better is a worker who has abundance of everything than someone who goes about boasting but lacks bread.

**28** My child, hold yourself in esteem with humility, and value yourself at your true worth.

**29** Who will acquit a person who sins against himself? And who will honor a person who dishonors his own life?

**30** A poor person is honored for his knowledge, and a rich person is honored for his wealth.

**31** One who is honored in poverty — how much more so in wealth! And one who is dishonored in wealth — how much more so in poverty!

---

## Council Notes

**On v.12 — "the beginning of human pride is to forsake the Lord":** The central theological declaration of the chapter. All agents preserved it faithfully. Ben Sira's anthropology: pride is not merely a moral failing — it is fundamentally a theological defection, a turning away from the Creator. SOPHIA retains the active verb "forsake."

**On v.13 — "root of sin":** EMET has "beginning of pride is sin"; LOGOS "pride is the source of sin"; PNEUMA "pride is sin's starting point." Greek archē hyperēphanias = "beginning of arrogance." "Root of sin" in SOPHIA captures both the theological image and its echo of 1 Tim 6:10 (love of money as "root of all evil"). Ben Sira may be the source of that tradition.

**On vv.14-17 — hymnic reversal:** Ben Sira celebrates God's overturning of the proud in hymnic language reminiscent of the Magnificat (Luke 1:52). SOPHIA preserves the parallel structure across all four verses.

**On v.19 — rhetorical questions:** The catechetical format (question-answer) is a distinctive wisdom device. LOGOS clarified the syntax best.

**On v.28 — "honor yourself with humility":** A deliberate paradox. True self-esteem is grounded in accurate self-knowledge, not self-inflation. LOGOS's phrasing is clearest.
